3. In their plaint, the plaintiffs disclosed their case stating inter alia that the Ka schedule property disclosed in the plaint originally belonged to Nezabot Ali Khan, Abdul Hakim and others and while they had been in possession of this land it was recorded in their favour during C.S. operation appertaining to khatian No.174 and Plot No.67 within Mouza Dhanmondi; Mirza Abdul Kadir one of the co-sharer of the Jamaindari Estate settled five bigas of land in favour of Sree Aboni Mohon Dey and Aboni Mohon executed a registered kabuliyat on 18-12-1940 and in course of such settlement Aboni Mohon being in possession of the said five bigas of land settled three bighas out of the same in favour of one Abdul Barek by a registered Addi Barga kabuliyat, subsequently, Aboni Mohon entered into an agreement for sale of one acres of land from the south western part of C.S. Plot No.67 with one Abdul Mazid Howlader and Begum Ayesha Noor on 29.07.47 at a consideration of Tk.3000/00 out of the said amount of Tlc.3000/00 the purchasers paid Tk.750/00 as earnest money whereupon possession was delivered in favour of the purchasers but due to partition of the country, the executant left for India so they subsequently arranged to execute and register a sale deed through an appointed attorney; meanwhile process of acquisition by the government was started through L.A. Case No.6 of 1948-49 in respect of part of Plot No.67; then one Sufia Khatun filed Writ Petition No.145 of 1965 challenging the notice issued in said L.A. Case and Rule was issued initially but subsequently the same was discharged on 19.08.1966 thereafter Sufia Khatun preferred an appeal to the Supreme Court of Pakistan being Appeal No.63-D of 1966 whereupon Pakistan Supreme Court vide its judgment and order dated 01.12.1967 allowed the appeal declaring the notice of acquisition as a defective one; it is also disclosed in the plaint that husband of Begum Aysha Nur was assured by the then C&B by its letter No.104 TP dated 15.01.53 for making construction on the suit property upon receipt of Government plan; thereafter, it is also stated in the plaint, that Ka schedule property along with some other properties were relieved from the acquisition process; on 26-10-56 one Ashutosh Dey Sarker being appointed as attorney of Aboni Mohon Dey executed and registered a sale deed in favour of Abdul Mojid Howlader and Ayesha Nur, thereafter Abdul Mojid Howlader transferred a area of 8 khatas of land from the suit plot in favour of one M. A. Goni and Afaiuddin Khan by a kabala dated 31.07.57 subsequently Mojid Howlader transferred the remaining 22 khatas of land by oral gift to predecessor of the 'plaintiffs Begum Ayesha Noor and since then Ayesha Noor had been possessing the schedule property till 03-10-2000 on which date she died leaving behind the plaintiffs as her legal heirs; the plaintiffs and their predecessors had been in possession of the suit property by constructing 16 shop rooms inducting tenants for more than 48 years and those shop rooms were rented in favour of different persons as tenants who had been running their business concerns in those rooms; while the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land as aforesaid RAJUK in collusion with the defendants demolished the structures constructed by the plaintiffs over the suit land and in the process RAJUK obtained an Aungikemama (bond) from the plaintiff No.1 under pressure; thereafter RAJUK again demolished the structures of the plaintiffs over the suit land by bulldozer in collusion with the husband of defendant No.6 with the aid of hired miscreants; after demolishing plaintiffs structures in the suit land on 30-03-2001 defendants dis-possessed the plaintiffs from the Ka schedule property by installing fencing with tin around it; they also constructed some rooms in the site; it is also stated in the plaint that the police did not take action against the influential invaders; lastly on 20.04.2001 a G.D. Entry could be made by the plaintiffs over the act of their dispossession on 30.03.2001. It is also stated in the plaint that the defendants are strangers who have dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land using RAJUK as a tool for their mischief. 

 4. Defendant Nos.1-6 entered appearance upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that one Gopeshor Paul was the C.S. recorded tenant of C.S. khatian No.174; he died leaving two sons Nil Kanta and Horn Krishna Paul; Hore Krishna died leaving only son Debraj Paul and Debraj Paul sold away 1.33 acres of land (three bighas by local measurement) including the structures thereon in favour of Kiron Chandra Banarjee on 17.07.33, thereafter on 18.04.48 Kiron Chandra transferred the said land to the predecessor of defendant Shahjahan Bhuiyan and immediately after his purchase 16.78 acres of suit C.S. Plot No.67 was acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.06 of 1948-49, compensation award was prepared in the name of Shahjahan Bhuiyan to the tune of Tk.3976.11 but the defendants predecessors did not withdrawn that compensation money as a result the said amount was deposited with the Government Revenue Account. It is also stated in the written statement that the said 1.33 acres of land of suit C.S. Plot No.67 remained in possession of the answering defendants since no formal possession was taken over by the L.A. Department.' The plaintiffs taking advantage of the land being vacant had illegally trespassed into a portion of the land and made some unauthorized construction which was subsequently demolished by RAJUK; the answering defendants have 14 semi pucca rooms in their portion of the land having been let out to different tenants; out of 4 bighas i.e. 133 acres of land these defendants am now in actual physical possession of 37 khathas encircled by C.I. sheet fencing and the remaining 43 khatha of land are in illegal possession of some unauthorized persons including the plaintiffs. These defendants are compelled to file suit for recovery of khan possession. it has also been specifically averred in the written statement that it appears on the face of the plaint that huge allegations have been made by the plaintiffs against the RAJUK and its officers but the RAJUK Chairman and other concerned officers have not been impleaded in the suit and no relief whatsoever have been sought for against the RAJUK and that under the Building Construction Act and the Rules framed thereunder RAJUK has its authority and statutory power to demolish unauthorized construction and in exercise of such power RAJUK with its Magistrate demolished the unauthorized structures and question of collusion and conspiracy with RAJUK by the answering defendants did never arise. It was also asserted in the written statement that the answering defendants inherited from their predecessor Shahjahan Bhuiyan a valid and good title in respect of the said 1.33 acres of land in suit C.S. Plot No.67 by virtue of inheritance from their predecessor Shahjahan Bhuiyan who purchased the same by virtue of a registered deed of sale dated 18.08.48 and that the claim of the plaintiffs is based on so called purchase in the year 1956 after acquisition of 16.78 acres of land in L.A. Case No.06 of 1948-49 is absolutely illegal and the present suit filed by the plaintiffs on the basis of the plaintiffs so-called claim is not entertainable in law, therefore, defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. Mr. Md. Ashadullah the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits at the outset that the description of the suit land as given in the plaint is vague in that the R.S. Plot and R.S. khatian numbers are different in Ka and Kim schedule of the plaint and that the Kalmi Naksha filed with the plaint and the plot number shown therein do not tally with the description of the Kha schedule land of the plaint, therefore, Mr. Ashadullah pointing out the provision of law i.e. Order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that in the absence of clear description of the suit land in the plaint the impugned decree is not sustainable and in substantiating Mr. Ashadullah placed reliance in the case of Nazrul Islam and others Vs. Santi Ram Duphi and others reported in 12 MLR (AD) 105.
